title: The Recordist Circuit — artboards and UI/UX option packs
status: Design proposal. Game runtime implementation awaits user selection.

artboards.initialPrompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: finished environment artboard for the game Chunk Surfer, titled only "THE RECORDIST CIRCUIT". Create one high-resolution landscape production concept-art sheet, approximately 3:2. This is a restrained psychological first-person game rendered as intricate black engraved linework, dense crosshatching, pale desaturated green-grey paper light, very selective amber practical lamps and phosphor-green recorder displays. Strong architectural scale and readable silhouettes, physically believable construction, no photoreal grading, no glossy fantasy. Layout: four beautifully composed environment panels with thin quiet gutters, one for each of these exact scenes, each scene large enough to read. Top left SNOWED-IN SCHOOL HALL: an ordinary school concert hall with much of the roof missing, snow drifts on rows of ordinary chairs, a clear central aisle, surviving warm stage lamps, a single school-aged boy seated quietly near the stage, a loose quarter-inch recording lead/tape lying from his chair toward an ordinary service door. No other people. Top right FIELD OF TAPE: magnetic tape unspooled over solid walkable ground like dead grass, physically slack suspended ribbons and a few immense metal tape reels in the distance, winding short paths rejoining, one recognisable ordinary timber service door on a threshold slab beyond the reels, no collectibles. Bottom left DEAD BROADCAST: a spacious pale plain with analog television interference restrained to distant surfaces, one robust transmitter mast with a small steady practical beacon, a low equipment shelter on a clearly traversable route and the onward door near the mast. No fullscreen flash, screens floating in space, cyberpunk, antenna forest, or hostile figures. Bottom right ASH WORKROOM: familiar institutional Ellery architecture partly buried in grey ash; a real surviving workroom with a lamp-lit worktable, practical cables, and one adult contractor seated with their BACK to camera, worn work coat, headphones, hands working near a compact black and brushed-metal DA1000 field recorder with small green stereo meters. The face stays turned toward the work, no dramatic portrait. The floor and door remain usable. Exactly the boy and the contractor in their separate scenes; no travellers or extra people. Precise small labels under panels only: "SCHOOL HALL", "FIELD OF TAPE", "DEAD BROADCAST", "ASH WORKROOM". Images dominate the artboard, typography restrained and immaculate. There is no game HUD, quest marker, progress bar, route counter, inventory loot, timer, arrows, visible player hands, weapons, monsters, or narrative exposition. Faithful to one committed 12–18 minute circuit which later returns to the exact school hall.

artboards.initialPrompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: finished performance and environmental-continuity artboard for the game Chunk Surfer, title only "THE SAME HALL, LATER". Create one high-resolution landscape production concept-art sheet, approximately 3:2. Style: physically convincing human anatomy and architecture translated into fine black engraved linework and deliberate crosshatching, desaturated pale green-grey light with restrained amber lamps and a small phosphor-green display. Never cartoony, not photorealistic painting, no glossy cinematic fog. The board consists of two large matching-camera panels across the upper two-thirds, and two beautifully drawn close-up studies along the bottom. Upper left panel labelled "BEFORE": an ordinary snowed-in school concert hall with missing roof, practical amber stage lamps still on, rows of worn school chairs and an open central aisle. One quiet school-aged boy seated near the stage, hands empty in lap; one distinctive chair foot is scuffed, a loose recording lead lies beside it. View from the back of the hall, human eye height, no visible player body or hands. Upper right labelled "RETURN": EXACTLY the same room geometry, camera position, chair positions, scuffed chair foot, lead and lamps. Now the adult contractor in worn work coat and headphones stands beside the boy, in three-quarter BACK view, passing a single compact DA1000 recorder to the boy. The adult's fingers are just releasing the real weight; the boy supports the recorder in both hands in his lap. Natural readable anatomy, neither figure looks at the viewer, no theatrical ghost poses, no identity revelation. Edges of some distant furnishings quietly lose engraved coherence, but the central floor and an ordinary softly lit exit door remain complete and useable. No falling roof, emergency chase or countdown. Lower left labelled "THE MACHINE": detailed scale-correct compact portable black and brushed-metal field recorder, DA1000 discreetly lettered, small green stereo level display, physical transport controls, ordinary screws, two familiar casing scratches and a worn strap lug; this is the identical machine being transferred above, not a suitcase, reel-to-reel deck or sci-fi scanner. Lower right labelled "TAKING ITS WEIGHT": close study of the same handover, adult hands releasing and child's hands supporting the SAME recorder, wrists and fingers anatomically correct, cable slack and cloth creases following weight. These close-up hands belong only to the contractor and boy; never show player hands. Exactly two people in the RETURN panel, only the boy in BEFORE. No other characters, weapons, monsters, HUD, captions beyond labels, objectives, timers or progress bars. Story remains ambiguous; art shows physical continuity, listening and a handover without explanatory words.
